1.title: Exam Technique and Final Review
1.text: Welcome to Module twenty-one: Exam Technique and Final Review. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do seven things. Time plan. The routine for every question. Domain checklists. Pairs the exam likes to confuse. Common traps. The final week. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All five domains. Exam format: up to ninety questions in ninety minutes; a score of seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred passes. Validated against: the official Comp T I A Security plus S Y zero eight oh one V eight exam objectives.

1.title: Time plan
1.text: Time plan. Maximum of ninety questions in ninety minutes: about one minute per question, with the performance-based questions (P B Qs) taking more. for the final V eight numbers. First pass. What to do: Answer quick questions; flag P B Qs and doubtful ones. Time: About fifty minutes. P B Qs. What to do: Do them after the quick questions: read the whole task, do what you can, never leave one blank. Time: About twenty-five minutes. Final pass. What to do: Review flagged questions; make sure every question has an answer. Time: About fifteen minutes.

1.title: Time plan, continued
1.text: Time plan. The figure shows this: A ninety-minute plan: quick questions first, P B Qs next, flagged questions last.

1.title: The routine for every question
1.text: The routine for every question. Read the last sentence first: what is asked? Mark the key words: B E S T, first, M O S T likely, L E A S T, not, E X C E P T. Name the domain and objective (control, threat, architecture, operations, governance). Remove options from the wrong category. Choose the answer that fits the constraint in the scenario (cost, time, law, availability). Choose-two or three questions: select exactly the number asked. Exam tip: Comp T I A often offers two plausible answers. The better one fits the exact scenario, the stated constraint and the question word (first step, best control, most cost-effective).

1.title: 1.0 General Security Concepts (16%)
1.text: one point zero General Security Concepts (sixteen percent). C I A, A A A, non-repudiation, Zero Trust, least privilege, defense in depth. Control categories (technical, managerial, operational, physical) and types (preventive, deterring, detective, corrective, compensating, directive). Change management: C A B, impact analysis, backout, maintenance window, documentation, version control. Cryptography: symmetric versus asymmetric, P K I, C S R, C R L versus O C S P, hash, salt, signature, key exchange, levels of encryption.

1.title: 2.0 Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Attacks (24%)
1.text: two point zero Threats, Vulnerabilities, and Attacks (twenty-four percent). C V E versus C V S S; threat feeds, likelihood and impact. Threat actors and motivations. Vectors: message, image, attachment, browser, network, remote, endpoint, supply chain, media, human, I O T, O T, physical, signal. Vulnerability types: unsupported, unpatched, zero-day, misconfiguration, hardcoded secrets, race conditions, shadow I T. Indicators: malware types, phishing family, D dos (distributed denial of service), on-path, credential attacks, injection, Io Cs. A I risks: poisoning, evasion, prompt injection, jailbreaking, hallucinations, data loss, bias, explainability.

1.title: 3.0 Security Architecture (19%)
1.text: three point zero Security Architecture (nineteen percent). Cloud, serverless, multicloud, I A C, O T, air gap, microservices, segmentation, data sovereignty. Zones and D M Z, device placement, fail open versus closed, Zero Trust, V P N (virtual private network), out-of-band, S S E. Data states, classification, masking, tokenization, hashing, data roles. Hot, warm, cold sites, redundancy, U P S and generator, backups (immutable), R T O, R P O, M T T R, M T B F.

1.title: 4.0 Security Operations (27%)
1.text: four point zero Security Operations (twenty-seven percent). Hardening, allow lists, honeypot family, I D S versus I P S, waff, U T M, E D R, X D R, D L P, N A C and eight oh two dot one X, S P F, dee kim, dee mark. Asset life cycle; vulnerability loop; C S P M (cloud security posture management), I P A M. sim, log aggregation, net flow, sys log, S N M P, scap, alert tuning. I A M: provisioning, federation (sam el, oh auth, L D A P (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol)), account types, M F A, access control models, J I T, passkeys. Automation versus orchestration, guardrails, agentic A I, C I or C D. Incident response phases, chain of custody, order of volatility, log and data sources.

1.title: 5.0 Program Management and Oversight (14%)
1.text: five point zero Program Management and Oversight (fourteen percent). Policy, standard, procedure, guideline; A U P, B Y O D, clean desk. Risk treatment (transfer, accept, avoid, mitigate); S L E times A R O equals A L E; risk register; B I A. R F I, R F P, R F Q; S L A (service level agreement), M O U, M O A, N D A, M S A, S O W; right to audit. Compliance, privacy rights, legal hold. Audits, pen test types, passive versus active recon, my ter attack. Awareness: initial, ongoing, targeted, corrective; B E C.

1.title: Pairs the exam likes to confuse
1.text: Pairs the exam likes to confuse. Detective versus corrective. finds an incident versus fixes the damage. Deterring versus preventive. discourages versus stops. Compensating versus corrective. substitute for a missing control versus repair after the event. Virus versus worm versus Trojan. needs a host versus spreads alone versus pretends to be useful. Spear phishing versus whaling. targeted at a person or group versus at executives. Brute force versus spraying. many passwords one account versus few passwords many accounts. I D S versus I P S. alerts versus blocks.

1.title: Pairs the exam likes to confuse, continued
1.text: Pairs the exam likes to confuse. C R L versus O C S P. list versus live query. Hashing versus encryption. one way versus reversible. sam el versus oh auth. authentication versus delegated authorization. R T O versus R P O. time down versus data lost. Poisoning versus evasion. corrupt the training versus fool the trained model. M O U versus M O A. non-binding versus binding. M S A versus S O W. umbrella terms versus one project. Tokenization versus masking. vault-backed substitute versus hidden display.

1.title: Common traps
1.text: Common traps. A longer, more complex answer is not always better: pick the one that answers the question asked. "first" often means contain or verify, not eradicate or recover. Encryption does not give integrity by itself; hashing does not give confidentiality. Backups must be tested and immutable copies protect against ransomware. Password plus P I N is not M F A (both are knowledge factors). Insurance transfers risk; it does not remove it. A self-signed certificate is not trusted by browsers. A policy is mandatory; a guideline is optional.

1.title: The final week
1.text: The final week. seven to five. One domain per day: read the cards and answer the recall questions from memory. four to three. The pairs table and the acronym list from the objectives, out loud. two. Redo all practice questions; list your misses and re-read those modules. one. Light review; check the test center or online rules and I D; rest.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Fabrikam Outdoors discovers that a workstation is sending data to an unknown server. What should the analyst do first? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Isolate the workstation from the network. Containment comes first: isolating the host stops the spread and preserves evidence.

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Which control best prevents a former employee's account from being used after they leave? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: Prompt deprovisioning. Disabling or removing the account at departure prevents stale accounts from being abused.

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. A company must recover from a site failure within two hours and pay the lowest possible cost. Which site is the best compromise? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Warm site. A warm site can restore in hours at a lower cost than a hot site.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Which action reduces the risk of ransomware destroying backups? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Immutable backups. Immutable backups cannot be altered or deleted for a set period.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. An asset worth two hundred thousand has a thirty percent exposure factor and a loss is expected once every two years. What is the A L E? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: thirty thousand. S L E is two hundred thousand times zero point three zero equals sixty thousand and A R O is zero point five, so A L E is thirty thousand per year.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. A user clicks a link in a text message and enters credentials on a fake page. Which attack and control pair is best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Smishing and security awareness training. A text-based phishing attack is smishing, addressed by awareness training and filtering.

2.title: Practice Question 7
2.text: Question seven. Which standard lets an application access a user's data on another service without receiving the user's password? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: oh auth. oh auth provides delegated authorization using tokens.

2.title: Practice Question 8
2.text: Question eight. A security team wants an early warning when someone browses to a fake finance folder. What should it use? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: A honeyfile. A honeyfile is a decoy that alerts when it is opened.

2.title: Practice Question 9
2.text: Question nine. A vendor contract should let the company check the vendor's controls at any time. Which clause is needed? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Right to audit. A right to audit clause allows inspection of the vendor's security.

2.title: Practice Question 10
2.text: Question ten. A developer's code review finds an A P I key written in the source. Which fix is best? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Move the secret to a managed vault and scan for secrets. Secrets should be stored in a vault, with scanning to prevent a repeat.

2.title: Practice Question 11
2.text: Question eleven. An executive receives an email that appears to come from the C F O asking for an urgent wire transfer. Which threat is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Business email compromise. Impersonating an executive by email to move money is business email compromise.

2.title: Practice Question 12
2.text: Question twelve. A tester has the network diagrams and credentials before testing. Which test type is this? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Known environment. Having full information is a known environment (white box) test.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. What is the passing score and scale? Answer: seven hundred fifty on a scale of one hundred to nine hundred. Question two. Which domain has the largest weight? Answer: Security Operations (twenty-seven percent). Question three. What do R T O and R P O measure? Answer: The maximum downtime and the maximum data loss, in time.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What is the order of the risk treatments? Answer: There is no order: transfer, accept, avoid and mitigate are four options. Question five. What do you read first in a question? Answer: The last sentence. Question six. What is new in V eight? Answer: More coverage of A I-related risks, security operations and modern environments.

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Time: up to ninety questions, ninety minutes; quick questions first, P B Qs next, flagged last. Method: last sentence, key words (B E S T, first, M O S T), domain, remove wrong category, fit the constraint. Biggest confusions: detective versus corrective, I D S versus I P S, sam el versus oh auth, R T O versus R P O, M O U versus M O A, M S A versus S O W, poisoning versus evasion. Traps: "first" equals contain, password plus P I N is not M F A, insurance transfers risk, test backups, self-signed is not trusted. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
